title: Forces and Energy: Formula Calculations
topic: Application of Forces and Transfer of Energy
subject: Science

questions.question: An object has a mass of 8 kg. What is its weight on Earth? (Use g = 10 N/kg)
questions.explanation: Weight = mass × gravitational field strength. W = mg = 8 kg × 10 N/kg = 80 N.

questions.question: A student lifts a 5 kg bag vertically through a height of 2 m. What is the gain in gravitational potential energy? (Use g = 10 N/kg)
questions.explanation: GPE = mgh = 5 kg × 10 N/kg × 2 m = 100 J. The bag gains gravitational potential energy as it is raised.

questions.question: A force of 30 N pushes a box horizontally for a distance of 4 m in the direction of the force. How much work is done?
questions.explanation: Work done = force × distance moved in direction of force. W = F × d = 30 N × 4 m = 120 J.

questions.question: A toy car of mass 0.5 kg moves at a speed of 4 m/s. What is its kinetic energy?
questions.explanation: KE = ½mv² = ½ × 0.5 kg × (4 m/s)² = ½ × 0.5 × 16 = 4 J. Remember to square the speed first.

questions.question: An object weighs 120 N on Earth. What is its mass? (Use g = 10 N/kg)
questions.explanation: Weight = mg, so mass = weight ÷ g. m = 120 N ÷ 10 N/kg = 12 kg.

questions.question: A crane does 600 J of work to lift a load vertically through 3 m. What is the weight of the load?
questions.explanation: Work done = force × distance. For vertical lifting, force = weight. So weight = work ÷ distance = 600 J ÷ 3 m = 200 N.

questions.question: A ball of mass 2 kg is dropped from a height of 5 m. What is its gravitational potential energy at the start? (Use g = 10 N/kg)
questions.explanation: GPE = mgh = 2 kg × 10 N/kg × 5 m = 100 J. This is the energy stored due to the ball's position above ground.

questions.question: A cyclist and bicycle have a combined mass of 60 kg. If they travel at 5 m/s, what is their kinetic energy?
questions.explanation: KE = ½mv² = ½ × 60 kg × (5 m/s)² = ½ × 60 × 25 = 750 J. Kinetic energy depends on mass and the square of speed.

questions.question: A student pushes a trolley with a constant force of 25 N. If 100 J of work is done, how far does the trolley move in the direction of the force?
questions.explanation: Work done = force × distance, so distance = work ÷ force. d = 100 J ÷ 25 N = 4 m.

questions.question: A book of mass 0.4 kg is placed on a shelf 1.5 m above the floor. What is the gravitational potential energy of the book relative to the floor? (Use g = 10 N/kg)
questions.explanation: GPE = mgh = 0.4 kg × 10 N/kg × 1.5 m = 6 J. Gravitational potential energy depends on mass, gravitational field strength, and height.
